source_text: Epistula synodalis Ἀμφιλοχίου ἐπισκόπου Ἰκονίου ἐπιστολὴ συνοδική. Καὶ πρὶν κομίζεσθαι τὰ παρὰ τῆς ἀγάπης ὑμῶν γράμματα, περιήγγειλεν εἰς ἡμᾶς ἡ φήμη καὶ τὸ τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν ἀκραιφνὲς καὶ πρὸς τοὺς κινδύνους παρατεταμένον καὶ πρὸς τὰ παθήματα τὰ ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ καρτερικὸν καὶ τῆς εἰς θεὸν ἀγάπης καὶ τὸ τῆς μελλούσης ἐλπίδος ἐν ὑμῖν βέβαιον. Ἐπεὶ δὲ καὶ τοῖς γράμμασι τῆς εὐλαβείας ὑμῶν ἐντετυχήκαμεν, εἴδομεν ὄντως ἐκκλησίας ἀποστολικῆς χαρακτῆρα καὶ ποιμένων ἀγαθῶν ζῆλον καὶ σπουδὴν ἄοκνον ἀληθινοῖς χριστιανοῖς πρέπουσαν. Τὸ γὰρ μήτε τῆς ὁδοῦ μῆκος ὑπολογίσασθαι μήτε διεσπασμένως τὰς πεύσεις προσα γαγεῖν, ἀλλὰ κοινῇ διὰ τῶν γραμμάτων ποιήσασθαι τὴν ἐρώτη σιν, λίαν ἡμᾶς εὐέλπιδας πεποίηκεν ὅτι συμφώνως ἐπιστείλαντες συμφώνως καὶ τὰς ἀποκρίσεις παρ' ἡμῶν δέξασθε· καὶ οἷόν τι προοίμιον τῆς τελειοτέρας ὁμονοίας τὴν ἐν τοῖς γράμμασιν ὑμῶν ὁμόνοιαν ἐδεξάμεθα. Καὶ δι' εὐχῆς μὲν ἦν ἡμῖν καὶ τὸν θαυμασιώ τατον καὶ μετὰ πάσης αἰδοῦς ὀνομαζόμενον ἐπίσκοπον Βασί λειον καὶ παρόντα δέξασθαι τῇ συνόδῳ καὶ κοινωνόν, μᾶλλον δὲ ἔξαρχον τῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς πραγμάτων ἔχειν. Ἐπεὶ δὲ ἐκεῖνον ἀρρωστία σώματος ὑπερβάλλουσα πρὸς τὴν ἄφιξιν διεκώλυ σεν, τελείας μέν ἐστιν ἀγάπης ὑμῶν μήτε τὰ τῆς ἡμετέρας βραχύτητος παριδεῖν γράμματα. Οὐ μέντοι τὴν ἁγίαν ὑμῶν ἐκκλησίαν ἄμοιρον καὶ τῆς ἐκείνου φωνῆς περιείδομεν· ἀλλ' ἔχοντες αὐτοῦ σύγγραμμα περὶ ταύτης ἰδικῶς αὐτῷ τῆς ὑποθέσεως πεπονημένον κἀκεῖνον διὰ τοῦ γράμματος ἔχομεν ἡμῖν συμφθεγγόμενον. Τίς οὖν ἡ πρὸς τὴν πεῦσιν ἀπόκρισις;
thought_title: Opening praise and the question of the Spirit
orientation: Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium, opens a synodal letter to fellow bishops, praising their faith and their joint inquiry, and noting that Basil's treatise on the Spirit is being sent with the letter.
pass_a_gloss: Synodal letter of Amphilochius bishop of Iconium, a synodal letter. And before the letters from your love were received, report announced to us both the purity of your faith and its being stretched toward dangers and its being steadfast toward the sufferings for Christ and the firmness in you of the love toward God and of the coming hope. But since we have also encountered the letters of your piety, we saw truly the character of an apostolic church and the zeal of good shepherds and an unwearying diligence befitting true Christians. For the fact that you neither reckoned the length of the road nor brought the inquiries separately, but in common through the letters made the question, has made us very hopeful that having written in harmony you will also receive in harmony the answers from us; and as a kind of prelude of the more perfect concord we received the concord in your letters. And it was in our prayer both to receive the most wonderful and with all reverence named bishop Basil also present at the synod and to have him as a sharer, or rather as leader of the matters toward you. But since an excessive weakness of body prevented him from the arrival, it is of your perfect love not to overlook even the letters of our smallness. Yet we did not leave your holy church without a share also of his voice; but having his treatise about this very subject labored over by him, we have him also speaking together with us through the writing. What then is the answer to the inquiry?

choices.why: The adjective describes the unmixed, unadulterated quality of their faith; 'purity' keeps the force of the adjective as a noun of quality.
The perfect passive participle conveys an ongoing state of tension or extension toward dangers; the passive force is preserved.
The adjective denotes patient endurance under suffering; 'steadfast' captures the active endurance rather than mere passivity.
The perfect tense indicates a completed action with present relevance; 'encountered' preserves the sense of meeting with the letters.
The term denotes one who leads or takes the lead in a matter; 'leader' is plain and keeps the contrast with 'sharer'.
The abstract noun denotes the lowliness or insignificance of the writer; 'smallness' is literal and preserves the self-deprecating tone.

pass_b_english: A synodal letter of Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium. Even before your letters arrived from your love, report had reached us of the purity of your faith, how it is being stretched toward dangers and is steadfast amid sufferings for Christ, and how firm in you is love for God and hope for the future. And now that we have encountered the letters of your reverence, we have truly seen the character of an apostolic church and the zeal of good shepherds, an unwearying diligence befitting true Christians. For you did not reckon the length of the road, nor did you bring your inquiries separately, but you made your request together through your letters. This has made us very hopeful that, having written with one accord, you will also receive our answers with one accord; and we received the harmony in your letters as a kind of prelude to a more perfect unity of mind.

It was our prayer to welcome to the synod the most admirable bishop Basil, who is named with all reverence, and to have him as a sharer—or rather as the leader—in our dealings with you. But since an overwhelming bodily illness prevented him from coming, it is a mark of your perfect love that you did not overlook even the letters of our smallness. Yet we have not left your holy church without a share in his voice either. Since we have a treatise of his composed specifically on this very subject, through that writing we have him speaking together with us. What, then, is the answer to your inquiry?

problems.quote: how it is being stretched toward dangers
problems.why: 'Stretched toward dangers' is awkward; likely means 'extended into dangerous situations' or 'tested by dangers'.
problems.fix: Revise to 'extended into dangers' or 'tested amid dangers'.

edits.old: how it is being stretched toward dangers
edits.new: how it is extended into dangers

fixed: Changed 'how it is being stretched toward dangers' to 'how it is extended into dangers' to better render παρατεταμένον, which means 'stretched out' or 'extended' toward dangers.
